summary: Opening Academy splash introduces Reach and Resolve as a paired doctrine whose familiar wording conceals two different ways a civilization can fail.
panelPlan: Single full-page opening splash: the doctrine seminar is already in session, with Merin on the floor among four cadets and a broad route map split between connected worlds and isolated settlements.
Integrate the complete title and opening copy into deliberate negative space without turning the page into a poster detached from the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Every cadet can repeat the words.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This course is about what happens when the words stop agreeing.

directionInline: Treat all CAPTION entries as exact integrated opening typography.
The page must feel like the first moment of a dramatic seminar, not a textbook title card.
No environmental readable text beyond the supplied copy.

summary: Merin opens by asking which half of the doctrine actually kept civilization alive, baiting the class into the safe answer.
panelPlan: Wide classroom panel with Merin holding two old physical route tokens, one intact and one deliberately darkened.
Medium on Oren answering from a carefully prepared slate while Jo glances sideways at him.
Close on Merin, neither approving nor correcting him.

dialogueInline.text: Which one kept us alive? Reach or Resolve?

summary: The cadets immediately fracture the slogan along regional experience: connection can mean survival, dependence, intrusion, or simply one more clock running out.
panelPlan: Jo leans forward over the route map and taps an isolated Verge cluster rather than looking at Merin.
Senn turns the intact route token in one hand while questioning who controls the route.
Nadi pulls the discussion back to a timing display showing reserves declining.
Merin watches the disagreement become useful.

dialogueInline.text: Depends who was doing the reaching.

summary: Merin moves the class into the archive lab and assigns two linked cases from the first multiworld rescue vessel launched after the Resolve Circle.
panelPlan: Transition into the archive lab as Merin places a battered early-relief route packet on the central table.
The projection resolves into the unfinished first rescue vessel seen at the end of Shattering, preserving its mismatched construction and unresolved command lineage.
Two destination lights appear on the route reconstruction: Orison and Varda.
End on the cadets reading the same mission brief from different sides of the table.

dialogueInline.text: First rescue vessel out of the Resolve Circle.
Same ship. Same week. Opposite mistakes.

summary: The archive reconstruction drops into the prototype's first route, where Ava and Ruben discover that the next two settlements need incompatible kinds of help.
panelPlan: Wide inside the prototype: patched consoles, hand-carried route packets, and mixed-origin systems make the ship feel assembled under deadline.
Ava marks Orison as immediate life-support risk and Varda as dark but transmitting local power stability.
Ruben opens the cargo inventory and realizes they cannot fully supply both destinations.
End on the ship turning toward Orison.

dialogueInline.text: Orison is asking for couplers, food, and scrubber media.

summary: Orison looks orderly at first glance, but its entire survival model is still waiting for a network that no longer exists.
panelPlan: Establish Orison as a beautiful standardized habitat under visible strain: empty replacement racks, ration queues, and untouched fabrication space.
Mira checks an arrival board whose expected convoy times have been crossed out by hand again and again.
A technician presents a failed scrubber module that the habitat was designed to replace rather than rebuild.
A child carries a food tray past sealed hydroponic bays that were never sized to feed the station.

summary: When the prototype docks, Ruben discovers that Orison's celebrated standardization left almost no local repair authority or raw-material practice.
panelPlan: Cargo doors open to residents expecting finished replacement modules.
Ruben examines the failed scrubber beside an immaculate empty standardized rack.
Mira points toward the replacement slots as if the missing parts are the whole problem.
Ruben turns instead toward the dormant fabrication bay.

summary: Ava offers Orison both immediate relief and the less welcome cargo of seed stock, machine patterns, and training time.
panelPlan: Ava opens one cargo pallet of food and medical consumables; relief is tangible and desperately needed.
She opens the next pallet to reveal seed stock, raw feed material, and physical fabrication patterns.
Mira looks from hungry residents to tools that will not solve tonight.
Ruben starts laying out the failed scrubber for a local repair team rather than taking it back aboard.

dialogueInline.text: Then seed stock and machine patterns.

summary: Mira accuses the crew of turning emergency relief into conditions, while Ruben insists that leaving only consumables would recreate the same emergency.
panelPlan: Mira blocks a pallet being redirected from finished couplers toward raw fabrication stock.
Behind her, Orison residents unload food while a local team gathers around Ruben's opened scrubber assembly.
Ava keeps the manifest visible so the dispute is about finite cargo, not abstract virtue.
End on Mira looking at the first locally machined replacement piece coming off the dormant fabrication bay.

dialogueInline.text: You're holding back what we asked for.
I'm leaving you what we have.
I'm trying not to come back to the same emergency.

summary: Back at the Academy, Jo sees Resolve in the Orison response while Oren objects that relief became coercive the moment outsiders decided what the habitat should become.
panelPlan: The Orison reconstruction freezes on food unloading beside the first locally fabricated part.
Jo points to the fabrication bay while Oren points to the withheld finished cargo.
Senn watches Merin rather than joining either side.
Merin closes Orison's file and opens Varda's.

dialogueInline.text: That's a relief crew deciding how Orison should live.

summary: Varda appears to be the success Orison was not: fed, powered, repaired, locally manufactured—and deliberately disconnected.
panelPlan: Wide establishing view of Varda's productive civic space: food growing, workshops, locally made machinery, and residents moving with practiced self-sufficiency.
A dark route receiver stands beside a locally built communications mast.
Eshen signs off on a repaired pump using a hand-kept tolerance book.
In the far distance, the prototype rescue vessel appears but does not cross the marked landing boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: Offworld ship is holding outside the line.

summary: Ava requests docking only to exchange updated route and engineering data; Eshen refuses because Varda's survival began by stopping trust in external systems.
panelPlan: Split the page between Eshen at Varda's physical boundary station and Ava aboard the prototype; neither side is visually dominant.
Ava keeps the request narrow: data exchange and inspection, no transfer of authority.
Eshen looks past the comm screen toward graves or a memorial wall built from early corridor-loss names.
The landing field remains empty.

dialogueInline.text: We have newer route drift and component tables.
You don't have to take us.
We buried everyone who trusted a green light.

summary: The prototype detects a debris migration that will soon narrow Varda's only safe launch volume, but the settlement refuses external navigation authority.
panelPlan: Ava overlays current drift measurements against Varda's older locally maintained route model.
Ruben sees the mismatch widening toward the settlement's only launch volume.
Ava transmits the raw measurements rather than an order.
Eshen receives the packet but leaves it unopened beside his local route book.

summary: The relief crew considers crossing Varda's boundary to inspect the route receiver, then rejects forced help even as the margin shrinks.
panelPlan: Ruben studies the landing boundary and the dark receiver through the forward view.
Ava lays the time-to-debris estimate beside the explicit refusal message.
A small boarding team waits for a decision but never launches.
End on the prototype holding position outside the line while the clock runs.

dialogueInline.text: We could be on that receiver in ten minutes.
Then we keep sending the numbers.

summary: Varda's locally manufactured pump fails not because local engineering is poor, but because years of isolated measurement drift have moved its tolerances away from the surviving external standard.
panelPlan: A critical pump begins vibrating violently in the maintenance hall.
Eshen and local technicians strip it quickly and competently, revealing a replacement bearing that looks correct by their own book.
A micrometer comparison against an old preserved external gauge reveals accumulated calibration drift.
Eshen looks toward the unopened external component table on the bench.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: We don't use that scale anymore.

summary: Varda asks for data rather than rescue; the prototype responds with full repair tables and the route model without demanding docking rights.
panelPlan: Eshen opens the previously rejected packet and sends a short return request from the boundary station.
Ava receives it aboard the prototype and immediately expands the transfer to include raw measurements and provenance.
Ruben adds field notes explaining which tolerances can safely vary and which cannot.
No shuttle launches; the exchange happens across the boundary.

dialogueInline.text: Sending the table and the raw measurements.
I'm adding failure limits. Don't ignore those.

summary: After repairing the pump and correcting its launch model, Varda sends back a locally developed repair method the prototype does not have, turning one-way assistance into exchange.
panelPlan: Varda machines a corrected bearing using the external tolerance reference while retaining its own local fabrication method.
The pump returns to stable operation.
Eshen records a Varda field repair for a casing fracture that the prototype's standardized table marks only as replace.
Ava receives the return packet aboard the ship; Ruben smiles despite himself.

dialogueInline.text: Your table says replace the casing.
Sending you what we do instead.

summary: The Academy returns to the paired cases, where Senn identifies the Varda exchange as Reach without physical entry or political incorporation.
panelPlan: The two case projections sit side by side: Orison's reopened fabrication bay and Varda's still-empty landing field.
Senn stands between them rather than on either side.
Oren studies the dark Varda landing field with visible surprise.
Merin lets Senn state the point.

dialogueInline.text: They reached Varda without entering it.

summary: Merin names the paired failure plainly: Orison had connection without independent capacity; Varda had capacity without exchange.
panelPlan: Merin places the intact route token over Orison and the dark token over Varda.
Jo moves the tokens away from a simple left-right opposition and overlaps them at the center of the map.
Nadi brings up survival timelines showing both settlements approaching failure for different reasons.
End on Oren realizing neither case is the 'good' example.

summary: The class argues over whether aid may ever carry requirements and whether refusal remains sovereign when delay threatens lives.
panelPlan: Jo points to Orison's consumption curve and argues that unrestricted relief would have repeated the dependency.
Senn points to Varda's boundary and argues that survival does not erase consent.
Nadi puts the debris clock between them.
Merin refuses to settle the dispute for them.

dialogueInline.text: If you keep bringing finished parts, they never build the shop.
If you force the shop on them, it's not theirs.
If the pump fails tonight, none of that matters.

summary: Merin removes the historical answer and turns the cases into a live simulation: one ship, two settlements, insufficient cargo, one refusal to land.
panelPlan: Historical projections collapse into a neutral simulation with altered names and no visible outcome.
A cargo inventory appears physically limited: food, medical media, raw feed stock, one fabrication head, and one navigation packet.
One simulated settlement requests everything; the other refuses landing but faces a moving route hazard.
Merin steps back and starts the clock.

dialogueInline.text: Forty-seven minutes to the first route loss.

summary: The cadets assemble a compromise that separates help from obedience: immediate consumables, local-production tools, raw data to the refusing settlement, and transparent handoffs rather than jurisdictional conditions.
panelPlan: Oren allocates emergency consumables while Jo redirects part of the cargo to the fabrication head and raw feed stock.
Senn creates a neutral unmanned transfer point outside the refusing settlement's boundary.
Nadi transmits raw route measurements with confidence bands rather than a command course.
The four cadets realize their plan still depends on the corridor remaining usable long enough for another contact.

dialogueInline.text: And the fabrication head. Not all finished parts.
No forced landing. Put the transfer outside their line.
Send the route data raw. Let them choose the course.

summary: Merin changes one assumption after the cadets think they have solved the exercise: the corridor may never reopen, forcing them to define the purpose of connection and self-sufficiency together.
panelPlan: Merin removes the future-resupply line from the simulation with one quiet gesture.
The cadets' carefully balanced plan suddenly shows a permanent break rather than a delay.
Nadi looks at the local-production package; Senn looks at the still-open communications channel.
End on the two route tokens from the first page now sitting together in the center of the table.

dialogueInline.text: Then we leave them something that works without us.
And something that lets them call us anyway.

summary: Closing teaser turns from survival after disconnection to the opposite danger: what happens when reconnection begins reshaping the people being connected.
panelPlan: Single full-page closing image: a modern green corridor opens between a polished Core docking standard and a smaller locally built port whose old hardware is already being removed for compatibility.
Merin appears only as a small figure observing the case image from the darkened Academy floor.
Reserve clean space for the exact teaser copy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It can also begin deciding the shape of the world it connects.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rex Fleet Academy: Reach and Resolve — Issue 2

directionInline: Treat CAPTION entries as exact integrated teaser typography.
Do not depict the Core standard as obviously villainous or the local port as obviously superior; the tension is interoperability versus autonomy.
